transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-28 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jared Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Zenith Head of AI), Tom Reynolds (Zenith Platform Eng), Ana Morales (Zenith Data Privacy Counsel)

Summary: quick scoping call; focusing on picking an open model and deciding deployment mode.

00:00:05 Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we, uh, appreciate you taking the time. quick intros?
00:00:12 Priya Kapoor: yeah hi i'm priya, head of ai at zenith, we run internal models for risk and client summarization, thanks.
00:00:18 Tom Reynolds: tom, platform eng, i'll be the infra point and cost gatekeeper.
00:00:22 Ana Morales: ana, data privacy counsel, i'll flag any data residency/privacy constraints.
00:00:28 Maya Chen: cool, from redwood, i'm maya, ae, and jared here is our se who'll go deeper on perf and security.
00:00:35 Jared Ortiz: hey all.

00:02:10 Maya Chen: ok high level, you're evaluating hosted v dedicated v private? what's driving the decision today?
00:02:18 Priya Kapoor: main drivers are: latency for interactive summarization for client managers, cost for volume batch runs, and strict residency for certain client docs. also we need longer context for multi-doc exec summaries - we're looking into 64k for some workflows.
00:02:40 Maya Chen: great, that's exactly what redwood is built for - we can run hosted to get started, dedicated reservation for predictable throughput, private for residency. each has tradeoffs, obviously latency/cost/privacy.
00:03:05 Tom Reynolds: quick question on models: open models look attractive for cost. what's your guidance on Mistral, Llama variants, Falcon? any redwood-verified perf numbers?
00:03:18 Jared Ortiz: yeah so we maintain a model catalog — we validate Mistral, Mistral Large, Llama 3 variants, Mixtral, Falcon 180b community runtimes, etc. for 64k context candidates, there are tuned variants; we also do quantized builds. note: not all open models have production 64k kernels yet, and some need more memory so latency increases.
00:03:45 Priya Kapoor: when you say "not all" do you mean we might see big latency jumps or just degraded perf?
00:03:52 Jared Ortiz: both, could be 2-4x token latency at 64k on same hardware vs 4k context. also batch sizes and KV caching matter - we do prefix caching which helps for repeated contexts, but first pass cost is higher.
00:04:20 Tom Reynolds: can we get some numbers? rough tokens per second on our expected GPU types?
00:04:26 Jared Ortiz: yes, maya will share our perf matrix; i can run bench on your sample corpus - we'll test 4k/32k/64k on Mistral-large, Llama3-13B, Mixtral and a Falcon variant. expect throughput drop off at 64k but some models are optimized.
00:05:05 Maya Chen: noted. next, multilingual: priya said en/es/jp — any language quality thresholds or is english-first?
00:05:15 Priya Kapoor: english-first but spanish needs high fidelity for customer communications and japanese for internal compliance docs - we need to verify that hallucination rates are acceptable.
00:05:28 Jared Ortiz: most open models handle spanish okay; japanese can be hit or miss depending on tokenization. we recommend running targeted evals. redwood optimize can suggest quantization/profile per workload to improve cost while maintaining quality.
00:05:50 Ana Morales: backed-up question on PII — if we do hosted, does redwood persist prompts or do you have opt-outs for retention?
00:05:58 Maya Chen: good question, by default hosted stores minimal metadata for billing and observability; for regulated data you can choose private deployment or dedicated with retention policies. we also support KMS integration for private key control.
00:06:20 Ana Morales: do you support HSM/KMS BYOK?
00:06:24 Jared Ortiz: yes, private deployments integrate with customer KMS/HSM. for hosted we offer managed KMS, but enterprise private supports BYOK.

00:08:05 Tom Reynolds: about tool-calling — we need secure retrieval from a vector DB and ability to invoke internal services (like a client-data lookup) without exfiltrating raw content. what's the pattern?
00:08:16 Jared Ortiz: two patterns: function/tool calling for structured outputs and an internal retrieval layer that stays in VPC. for hosted we use proxies and redwood routing; for private the retrieval stays within customer network. we also support signed tool calls and per-route RBAC.
00:08:40 Priya Kapoor: does function calling mean like OpenAI-style function calls or Redwood has a different contract?
00:08:46 Jared Ortiz: similar concept — we support structured tool calling and also have first-class support for streaming function responses. some models have native function call heuristics we map to. be aware that some open models don't have deterministic function calling behavior and need a shim in the runtime.

00:10:10 Maya Chen: on the deployment side, if you need residency for certain documents, we usually propose a hybrid: hosted for non-sensitive and private/dedicated for sensitive subsets. reduces cost but keeps control.
00:10:25 Tom Reynolds: makes sense. capacity-wise, what does dedicated look like? is it per-GPU reserved or pool-based?
00:10:33 Jared Ortiz: dedicated is pool-based with reserved capacity and autoscale settings. you can configure burst to hosted if you want overflow — reduces cold-start risk. SLA and latency targets are explicit in dedicated.

00:12:00 Priya Kapoor: latency targets — we need sub-800ms p95 for short prompts (single-doc summarization) and <2s for 8k+ prompt interactions. achievable?
00:12:12 Jared Ortiz: for short prompts on optimized models on dedicated hardware, yes sub-800ms p95 is feasible. for 64k contexts you'll likely be in the 1.5-3s range depending on model/hw; that's why we want to bench.

00:14:20 Tom Reynolds: cost model question: with open models + quantization + batching, what's typical cost delta vs closed models?
00:14:28 Jared Ortiz: big variance. quantized Mistral or Llama3 on dedicated can be 30-60% cheaper per token versus large GGML-like setups; hosted convenience factors in. we'll include per-token and per-embedding breakout in the cost sheet.

00:17:02 Priya Kapoor: about evals — can you help run an A/B with our prompts comparing hallucination rates and rouge/accuracy metrics?
00:17:10 Jared Ortiz: yes we do quality monitoring and can run evals tied to prompt sets, and Redwood Optimize will flag regressions. we can instrument metrics for hallucination proxies.

00:19:30 Ana Morales: legal needs to see data flow diagrams and proof of no log retention for certain flows. can you provide that?
00:19:37 Maya Chen: absolutely — we'll include a data flow diagram and a privacy config doc. for private we can restrict logging entirely to customer logs.

00:22:00 Tom Reynolds: one last technical: KV cache — is that per-request or per-session; we want to reuse across repeated context fragments to save compute.
00:22:10 Jared Ortiz: we support prefix/KV caching and session affinity; you can cache embeddings or KV tokens to reduce repeated work. note there are consistency tradeoffs when you update context frequently.

00:24:55 Priya Kapoor: ok good, so immediate next steps?
00:25:02 Maya Chen: recap: maya will send perf matrix and security pack; jared will run bench with our sample; priya will share prompts and languages; ana will confirm legal constraints. then we'll have pricing call for dedicated.
00:25:21 Tom Reynolds: timeline wise we want a pilot by mid-June if possible, at least a small POC.
00:25:29 Maya Chen: that's doable if we get the sample corpus and access to someone to run bench.

00:27:00 Priya Kapoor: quick note — for japanese docs we have some legacy encodings, is that something that trips tokenizers?
00:27:08 Jared Ortiz: sometimes, especially with fullwidth punctuation and legacy line breaks; we can normalize in the preprocessor. we'll include guidance.

00:30:00 Ana Morales: security quick clarifier: if we go hybrid, how do you ensure no accidental routing of sensitive flows to hosted?
00:30:08 Jared Ortiz: routing policies are per-route and we support model pinning and mandatory private-only tags for certain routes. we'll show the console rules.

00:35:15 Maya Chen: any other blockers?
00:35:22 Tom Reynolds: pricing and procurement — need ballpark committed rates for dedicated monthly, and details on termination/commit.
00:35:30 Maya Chen: we'll include an indicative pricing sheet, and procurement/legal will follow up.

00:40:00 Priya Kapoor: one more thing — tool-calling security: can we run tool call handlers inside our VPC and have Redwood only pass pointers?
00:40:08 Jared Ortiz: yes, that's a common pattern for private deployments — Redwood runtime can hand back a signed pointer and your service resolves it internally. we'll document the flow.

00:45:00 Maya Chen: ok we are at ~45 minutes, let's do final recap and owners.
00:45:05 Maya Chen: recap: Maya share perf matrix + security pack + pricing; Jared: bench tests; Priya: prompts & sample corpus; Ana: legal constraints; Tom: coordinate finance for pricing deep-dive.
00:45:30 Priya Kapoor: sounds good.
00:46:00 Tom Reynolds: thanks, we'll aim to have the sample corpus to you by Tue 2026-06-02.
00:46:10 Maya Chen: perfect, we'll target pricing call week of 2026-06-08.
00:46:20 Ana Morales: i'll follow up on legal whitepaper.
00:46:30 Maya Chen: great thanks everyone.
00:46:35 Jared Ortiz: thanks, bye.
00:46:38 (call ends)
